memory_candidates.content: When a markdown command/skill recipe's git-commit-scoped.sh call site needs an explicit pathspec but the recipe's real write set is inherently dynamic (which directories moved, whether a conditional step fired), replace a bare directory pathspec with a `stage_paths` bash-array accumulator built through the recipe's own preceding steps and referenced as `-- "${stage_paths[@]}"` at the commit, rather than forcing a static enumerated list that will drift. Verified empirically that `git add <old_path> <new_path>` (no trailing slash, passing both the removed source and the new destination of one `mv`) correctly records a rename rather than leaving the deletion unstaged -- useful for staging a directory rename pair without a bare recursive directory pathspec.

A regex/line-oriented lint classifying pathspec tokens as task-scoped vs shared-directory should recognize THREE forms of task-scoping, not just `${...}` interpolation and `{N}`/`{NNN}` template placeholders: a worked/rendered example may show a literal, already-substituted task number (e.g. `specs/427_some-slug/reports/`), which looks shared under a naive check but is actually task-scoped. Match this with a `/[0-9]+_` directory-segment-prefix regex, mirroring the `{NNN}_{SLUG}` naming convention.
